result:
If I could change one thing, I’d make a certain kind of education universal—free, lifelong, and built around critical thinking, empathy, and agency. Not just literacy or job skills, but practice in asking better questions, recognizing manipulation, understanding people unlike you, and believing you can actually shape your circumstances.

Most other problems—poverty, war, climate inaction, inequality, authoritarianism—aren’t unsolvable in principle. They persist because of information asymmetries, concentrated power, and a failure of imaginative empathy. If enough people could reason clearly and care widely, the pressure to fix those problems would become much harder to ignore.

It’s not a magic cure, and power would resist it. But it’s the change with the most leverage.
